assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_KUSUNOKI_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (27,914 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, veto false), a portrait of Commander Kusunoki in the Japanese TV series (E01-E13) and Friends Short 02. It locates her by episode, cue and timecode and by the project's ruling IDs (KUS-MB, REL), reads the E12 relay through the owner's 23 November listening return, and closes with 'Where her portrait holds'. The discovery row claims E01-E13 with Short 02. The portrait's React and Reload 02 sections are attributed comparisons outside the television continuity, and no prediction here rests on them. The ledgers, readings and recheck records it links are not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on them directly. The project's COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY outcome was not adopted as a grade. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Her history belongs to her at every state, so far as the portrait gives it: the time when LilyBell came to kill Chisato and she and Mika negotiated with their superiors (reported in E12), and a long working acquaintance with Mika. Located present states: the warehouse order, the Walnut order and the account of the breach (E01); private skepticism with her aide (E01-E02); the exercise and the denial of a promised return (E01, E03); the Majima drawings and Fuki's identification (E07); the camera and the rebuke to Chisato (E09); Majima's question, the no-fire order, and Itadori's order to use Chisato (E10); Takina's report (E11); the covert request through Mika and taking command after Itadori's withdrawal (E12); the order to withdraw from the tower, the gun count and the Hawaii call (E13). Short 02 is placed as the portrait places it, without a calendar. Nothing after E13; print stories are outside scope.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: 'Where her portrait holds' gives three conditional rules. After a failed operation that involves a protected fact, Kusunoki asks people she trusts for better information and limits what the affected girls may contest (E01-E03). Faced with an operative she cannot replace, she tries duty, debt, an imperative or an intermediary, and Chisato's refusal can still stand (E09, E10). When a superior is prepared to sacrifice her people, she has once helped without acknowledgment through someone outside headquarters (E12). The model predicts her mistakes: dismissing young witnesses whose effort later corrects her (E07), turning a dying girl's debt into a claim (E09), and leaving Takina no standard for a return (E01, E03). Not B: the portrait does not explain why her response changes. At both hinges it names competing motives and declines to choose. In E09 affection, recall and staffing could produce the same acts. In E12 preserving the institution, recovering her position and wanting Fuki and the others to live could all motivate the same call. Those motives would diverge in a new crisis, and the portrait says none of its conditions predicts that she will disobey every destructive order, and that we know less about what she wants for herself than about whom she will ask. That is insufficiency, not productive uncertainty. Not D: the instruments are located across E01-E13 and Short 02.

Located states: the LilyBell history she negotiated with Mika, reported later (E12); the E01 order and the account of the breach; private skepticism and self-criticism with her aide (E01-E02); the camera and the rebuke to Chisato (E09); the argument with Majima and Itadori's order (E10-E11); the covert request through Mika, then taking command in her own name after Itadori's withdrawal (E12); the order to withdraw from the tower and the Hawaii call (E13). The portrait says what changes is partly the viewer's chance to see her choose at different costs, and declines a late conversion. Not B: no inner transition is located, and the LilyBell history is reported, not shown. Not D: the states are located by episode and cue.

'A voice at the other end of the line' gives addressee-conditioned register with cues: doubt and the joint 'we' with her aide (E02); courteous お任せください to her superior (E10); ください and a brief どうも to Mika (E10, E12); Fuki's name used to stop an indiscretion, and 命令だ and refusing to say it twice when Fuki wants to continue (E03, E13); blunt imperatives to Chisato (E09, E10); the plainer 聞いてほしい when Chisato will not listen (Short 02); and remarking that Chisato looks well (E09) or sounds well (E13) before a demand or a work request. Not A: the sample is small, the portrait says it establishes nothing about pitch, breath or a performer's intention, and her words at the other end of the E13 call are unavailable. Not C: the register rules are stated per addressee and located.

The portrait says the series gives her scarcely any independent leisure, domestic routine or bodily self-description. Located only: calling the radio tower an eyesore (E01) and trying to finish a call to operatives who are not listening (Short 02). Not D: there is nothing beyond these two moments.

Directed differences: her aide (candor and self-criticism, E01-E02); Itadori (polite requests for discretion, then carrying his demand downward, E10); Mika (a channel for a favor that could compromise them both, trusted to withhold her name, E10, E12); Fuki (a name that silences, an order she will not repeat, and the girl she asks for by name when she takes command, E03, E12, E13); Chisato (blunt imperatives, debt, the returned camera, a refusal she cannot overturn, E09, E13); Takina (no promise of return, a pertinent follow-up that still sends her back to the operation, E01, E11); Majima (an articulate defense of DA, E10). Not A: the history with Mika is only partly given and she has no private relationships on screen. Not C: each relationship has located states and a stated difference.

Located only: the tower as an eyesore (E01), wanting the hacker and the information gone while declining to trust the rumor (E02), and 'we have lost our edge' (E02). The portrait says we know less about what she wants for herself than about the people from whom she will risk asking something, and it does not know whether she understood what the camera meant to Chisato. Not D: there are no stated motives for her central choices.

Located modes with outcomes: silencing Fuki with her name and calling the failure technical (E03); denying she promised Takina a return (E01); pressing Chisato with debt and an order to sit, which Chisato refuses (E09); defending DA to Majima and promising he can disappear from memory (E10); asking Itadori for discretion, then carrying his order downward (E10); acting covertly through Mika against the upper order (E12); ordering withdrawal and refusing to say it twice (E13). Not A: she never openly defies a superior, and the portrait says none of its conditions predicts that she will disobey every destructive order. Not C: the modes are varied, located and conditioned on the addressee's power.

Located positions: wanting witnesses alive and waiting for Chisato (E01); keeping the breach secret and letting Takina's independent action stand as the account (E01); DA's legitimacy from its history and from a peace in which people do not feel the presence of malice (E10); forbidding fire on armed civilians when exposure is Majima's object, which the portrait says is not a principled aversion to killing (E10-E11); helping the girls covertly (E12). Not B: she is never shown weighing alternatives, and the motive for the E12 choice is undetermined. Not D: her ideology is articulate and located.
The portrait does not establish humor or play for her. Short 02 is comic at her expense, and her dry greetings to Chisato (E09, E13) are read as rebuke, pleasure or relief, not as play.

One dedicated portrait covers E01-E13 and Short 02 with cue numbers, timecodes and ruling IDs, applies the owner's 23 November listening return to the E12 relay, and separates the two print comparisons. Not A: the row curates only this derived item, her screen time is limited, and the portrait claims no new native viewing or listening. Not C: every appearance and decision is located.

Located bounds against overreading: the E12 withdrawal is Itadori's order, relayed before she takes command; she is not a party to the second call threatening Chisato (E10); the no-fire prohibition under exposure is not a principled aversion to killing (E10-E11); the speaker who calls her a good person is unnamed in the caption (E12); whether she knew what the camera meant to Chisato is unknown (E09); there is no completed bargain at the E09 table; she did not secretly sanction the Takina-Fuki division of responsibility (E13); speculation about her and Mika proves nothing about her private life (E07); the authorship of the E01 report is omitted; and the print planter and memorial approval are not TV habits or policy. Not A: no forecast about her is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.
States are placed by episode, cue and timecode. Not B: there is no story calendar, the LilyBell history is undated, and Short 02 is undated. Not D: the episode states are precisely located.

conditions: Illustrative lines only, in the located registers: the joint 'we' with her aide, お任せください to a superior, ください and どうも to Mika, a name or 命令だ to Fuki, blunt imperatives to Chisato, and 聞いてほしい when an order is not heard (E02, E03, E09, E10, E12, E13, Short 02).
Excluded: private, intimate or leisure speech, and her words at the other end of the E13 call.
scenario_readiness.note: The discovery row claims speech, and the portrait gives addressee-conditioned register with cues. The register constrains illustrative command speech; pitch, breath and private speech are not established.

conditions: A failed operation that involves a protected fact: predict that she asks trusted people for better information and limits what the affected girls may contest (E01-E03).
An operative she cannot replace: predict duty, debt, an imperative or an intermediary, with the operative's refusal able to stand (E09, E10).
A superior's order that puts her people at risk, with a trusted outside actor available: predict covert help without acknowledgment (E12). This is observed once.
A challenge to DA's legitimacy: predict a defense from its history and from a peace without felt malice (E10).
After a rescue: predict that she still puts secrecy and her own orders first (E13).
Include her mistakes: dismissing witnesses whose work later corrects her, claiming a dying girl's debt, and offering no standard for a return.
Exclude open defiance of a superior, a destructive order with no outside actor available, her private wants, and any late conversion.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Television E01-E13 and Short 02. The LilyBell history she negotiated with Mika is in the past at every state. From E12 the girls know she can act for them covertly; her lawful command resumes only after Itadori's withdrawal. Nothing after E13.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Her aide, her superior Itadori, Mika as a trusted channel, Fuki as field leader, Chisato and Takina as operatives, and Majima as an adversary. A comparable new operative or superior is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: DA headquarters, field operations by radio and telephone, and the series' Tokyo.
No print scene, no private or domestic setting, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation follows the portrait's three conditional rules within DA. The motive that decides between institution, position and the girls' lives is not established, so a crisis where those diverge is excluded.
The portrait says the series gives her scarcely any independent leisure or domestic routine; social life outside command would be invented.

conditions: Predict her stated justification of DA: it predates the present law, has protected the country, and aims at a peace without felt malice (E10).
Predict the use of secrecy in both directions, against an operative's interests (E01) and against a superior's order (E12).
Excluded: the motive that decides a dilemma and any genuine weighing of alternatives.
scenario_readiness.note: Her ideology is located; her weighing is not.
The cafe group's speculation about her and Mika proves nothing about attraction or partners, and the portrait gives her no private life.

conditions: Command-room conduct: orders, briefings, a no-fire prohibition under exposure, and managing what is reported (E01, E10, E11, E13).
Managing operatives: tests without promises, pressure on an irreplaceable operative, recalls to the operation (E03, E09, E11).
Dealing with a superior: polite requests for discretion and carrying his demand downward (E10).
Excluded: her rise to command, DA's internal politics beyond Itadori, and the final report's authorship.
scenario_readiness.note: Her command conduct is the best-located part of the portrait.

known_limits.statement: The portrait leaves her motive open at both hinges: affection, recall and staffing in E09; the institution, her position and the girls' lives in E12.
None of the portrait's conditions predicts that she will disobey every destructive order, and Fuki hears her put secrecy first even after the rescue.
Following the owner's 23 November listening return, Itadori orders the E12 withdrawal; Kusunoki asks for Fuki and takes command only afterward.
She is not a party to the second call threatening Chisato and only asks whether someone else is there (E10).
Whether she knew what the returned camera meant to Chisato is unknown (E09).
Her given name, childhood, recruitment, rise to command and life at home are outside the portrait.
The LilyBell history is known only through Mizuki's account, and the speaker who calls her a good person is unnamed in the caption (E12).
Her words at the other end of the E13 call and her reaction to the holiday are unavailable; only Chisato's side is heard.
The React and Reload 02 scenes are attributed comparisons outside the television continuity and are not used for prediction.
Untested: open defiance of a superior, a destructive order with no outside actor available, and her response to Chisato's no-kill condition.
No humor or play of her own is established.
